questions.prompt: Which IETF RFC specification defines the modern Transport Layer Security protocol version 1.3 (TLS 1.3)?
questions.explanation: RFC 8446 (published in August 2018) specifies TLS 1.3, superseding TLS 1.2 defined in RFC 5246.

questions.prompt: How many network round-trips (RTT) are required for a standard full handshake in TLS 1.3 compared to TLS 1.2?
questions.explanation: TLS 1.3 optimizes latency by combining key share exchange with the ClientHello/ServerHello messages, cutting handshake latency to 1-RTT.

questions.prompt: Why did TLS 1.3 completely remove static RSA key transport in favor of Ephemeral Diffie-Hellman (ECDHE)?
options: RSA keys are too short for modern CPUs
RSA certificates cannot be signed by CAs
Diffie-Hellman eliminates the need for certificates
questions.explanation: With static RSA, compromising the server private key allows retrospective decryption of all past sessions. Ephemeral Diffie-Hellman (ECDHE) generates fresh per-session keys to guarantee Perfect Forward Secrecy.

questions.prompt: Which component of the TLS architecture is responsible for negotiating cipher suites and establishing session keys?
questions.explanation: The TLS Handshake Protocol handles cipher negotiation, server/client authentication, and key agreement before the Record Protocol encrypts application data.

questions.prompt: What cryptographic object protects against Man-in-the-Middle (MITM) attacks during the ServerHello phase?
options: An X.509 Digital Certificate signed by a trusted Certificate Authority (CA)
questions.explanation: The server presents an X.509 certificate carrying its public key, digitally signed by a trusted CA. The client validates the signature chain to authenticate the server.

questions.prompt: Which symmetric encryption mode family is exclusively mandated in TLS 1.3, removing older CBC-mode ciphers?
options: AEAD (Authenticated Encryption with Associated Data, e.g., AES-GCM)
questions.explanation: TLS 1.3 eliminated CBC-mode ciphers (which were prone to padding oracle attacks like POODLE and Lucky13) and mandates AEAD ciphers such as AES-GCM and ChaCha20-Poly1305.
